title: Clear Street launches electronic execution across Europe and Asia Pacific
summary: Clear Street ("Clear Street" or "the Company"), a cloud-native financial infrastructure technology firm on a mission to give every sophisticated investor access to every asset in every market, today announced the launch of electronic execution in Europe and Asia-Pacific, extending its algorithmic trading offering beyond the US and Canada for the first time.
content: Cloud-native financial infrastructure technology firm Clear Street has launched electronic execution services in Europe and Asia-Pacific. This expansion extends the company's algorithmic trading offering beyond the US and Canada for the first time, providing sophisticated investors with broader access to international markets.

content: August consumer confidence remained largely stable overall, according to data from The Conference Board. However, this headline stability masks a growing divergence in spending trends. title: The Corporate Bank Account Is Becoming an Event Stream
summary:
Corporate treasury typically works in sequence. Money moves, banks record it, statements arrive, and finance teams reconcile what happened. Fast forward to today, and that sequence is starting to run in reverse. As payments become faster and transaction data becomes richer, the economically useful moment is not when a balance changes or a statement closes. […]
The post The Corporate Bank Account Is Becoming an Event Stream appeared first on PYMNTS.com.
content: Corporate treasury is shifting away from traditional sequential processing toward real-time event streams. As payment speeds increase and transaction data grows richer, finance teams can process economically useful moments as they happen rather than waiting for statements to close and balances to change. This modern approach reverses the historical workflow of financial reconciliation.

Brad Garlinghouse says XRP has already cleared its legal hurdle. Ripple’s CEO pointed to a federal judge’s ruling from the company’s four-year fight with the SEC: XRP itself is not a security. “That is clarity for XRP,” Garlinghouse said. But he says that’s not enough. Ripple’s position is that the whole crypto industry needs the …
content: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse stated that XRP possesses legal clarity following a federal judge's ruling in the company's multi-year legal battle with the SEC, which established that the digital asset itself is not a security. However, Garlinghouse emphasized that this clarity must extend to the broader cryptocurrency industry rather than benefiting XRP alone, as the company continues advocating for comprehensive regulatory certainty.
